BladeNet achieves an average precision (AP) of 0.995 for blade detection on the Ørsted turbine blade inspection dataset.
BladeNet obtains an AP of 0.223 for blade detection on the transfer DTU NordTank dataset, outperforming other methods.
The PANDA semi-supervised anomaly detection method achieves the highest AUC of 0.639 on the Ørsted turbine blade dataset.
The Ørsted turbine blade inspection dataset contains 2637 high-resolution (6720 x 4480) drone images of offshore wind turbines.
The DTU NordTank dataset contains 1170 drone images of onshore wind turbines.
Wind turbine blades are typically made from Glass Fibre Reinforced Plastic (GFRP) materials.
Turbine blades are susceptible to operational and weather-based damage over time, reducing energy efficiency.
Prior supervised anomaly detection methods were limited to a few discrete classes of defects.
BladeNet's unsupervised blade detection stage isolates the blade regions from the background, improving anomaly detection performance.
BladeNet utilizes a U-Net architecture for one-class instance segmentation to accurately detect and extract turbine blades.
The paper evaluates several semi-supervised anomaly detection approaches including VAE, AnoGAN, GANomaly, Skip-GANomaly, and PANDA.
BladeNet's dual-module architecture requires minimal prior manual annotation of training data.
The authors use morphological operators and negative example sampling to create 'pseudo ground truth' for the blade detection model.
Simple Linear Iterative Clustering (SLIC) is used to generate super-pixel clusters on the extracted blade regions for anomaly detection.
BladeNet produces clean, sharp instance segmentation masks that closely fit the turbine blades, including important edge regions.
